newsitem.title: USA: Transco says cuts pressure in NY gas line.
newsitem.headline: Transco says cuts pressure in NY gas line.

text.p: Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line (Transco) said it is sharply cutting pressure in its 26-inch diameter natural gas pipeline on Staten Island, N.Y., as a precaution after a bomb scare earlier Wednesday.
"We're cutting pressure in the line to about 60 pounds (per square inch)," said company spokesman Chris Stockton.
The line usually operates at about 700 psi, he said.
Transco earlier said it did not anticipate any disruptions on the line, which is a lateral line tying into the Brooklyn Union gas delivery system.
Buckeye Pipeline Co shut its nearby petroleum products line after a suspicious package was found along the line.
Police and FBI agents are currently removing the package.
The Buckeye line runs north from Staten Island to John F Kennedy airport, on Long Island across the entrance to New York harbor.
Stockton said Transco has dispatched two crews to join police inspecting the gas line.
Traders said restricting the flow through Transco's line would likely have no impact on natural gas prices in New York City, where the weather is currently unseasonably mild.
